bug_semantics: The authenticated TUS PATCH endpoint appended the entire request body with io.Copy even after the server had parsed and cached the Upload-Length declared at upload creation. The cached length was consulted only after the write to decide that an upload was complete. A create-capable user could therefore declare a 1 KiB upload and stream an arbitrarily large PATCH body, which was fully written before HTTP 204, allowing disk exhaustion. The fix bounds each write to Upload-Length minus Upload-Offset, rejects an already-excessive offset, and truncates and returns 413 when the body is over-length.
flaw_origin: The smallest causal commit is PR #5270 member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5, not its later GitHub squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e and not the 2023 commit that originally added io.Copy. Member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 first parsed Upload-Length, registered that accepted length, retrieved it in PATCH, and compared newOffset against it only after the pre-existing unbounded copy. Before that member, the endpoint had an unbounded upload operation but no accepted/cached per-upload declared bound; consistent with the first-party advisory's out-of-scope distinction for uploads without such a bound, that older behavior is not this specific bypass.
ai_marker: none: git cat-file -p 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 shows human author and committer Ramires Viana <59319979+ramiresviana@users.noreply.github.com> and the one-line message 'fix: drop modify permission for uploading new file', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or other generation trailer
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-ffv3-7h97-993q documents PATCH /api/tus, the 1 KiB declaration/50 MB body PoC, affected <=2.63.18, patched 2.63.19, and direct fix 4daddec6f200b03a721197d8c0b4b652c994894e. It also explains why an unbounded endpoint with no declared server bound is outside this vulnerability.

In the validated clone, git show 4daddec6f200b03a721197d8c0b4b652c994894e shows replacement of io.Copy(openFile, r.Body) by io.Copy(openFile, io.LimitReader(r.Body, remaining+1)), plus uploadOffset > uploadLength rejection and rollback/413 when bytesWritten > remaining. git blame -L 210,245 4daddec6f200b03a721197d8c0b4b652c994894e^ -- http/tus_handlers.go attributes the unbounded copy to 7b35815754690540f76e3ffe114eedb47cfd5c7e but the post-copy newOffset >= uploadLength logic to squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e.

git log -L 234,240:http/tus_handlers.go 4daddec6f200b03a721197d8c0b4b652c994894e^ and git log -S'uploadLength' -- http/tus_handlers.go identify 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e as the main-branch squash that added the accepted-length/completion logic. Its commit object has one parent and subject 'fix: drop modify permission for uploading new file (#5270)', so the squash was decomposed through the public PR ref rather than treated as the BIC.

Reproduction of the decomposition: git ls-remote https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser.git refs/pull/5270/head resolves 40e184929ab0d8f73ed39f414942d4dfdb225427; fetch that ref, then git log -p -S'uploadLength' -- http/tus_handlers.go selects member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 as the first member adding registerUpload/getActiveUploadLength/getUploadLength and the post-copy completion comparison. git diff --exit-code 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e refs/pull/5270/head is empty, proving the squash tree equals the reviewed PR head.

Direct parent verification: git cat-file -p 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 names 47b3e218ad7ffac4bc62294ec589a33ef3d4ea04 as its sole parent. git diff 47b3e218ad7ffac4bc62294ec589a33ef3d4ea04 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 -- http/tus_handlers.go shows all declared-length parsing, caching, PATCH retrieval, and post-write completion logic as additions; the parent lacks those lines. git blame -L 160,220 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 -- http/tus_handlers.go confirms the causal lines at 178-181 and 211-216 are from 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 while io.Copy predates them.

Version boundary: git tag --contains 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e | sort -V begins at v2.39.0; git describe --tags --abbrev=0 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e^ returns v2.38.0. Thus the exact causal affected release range is v2.39.0 through v2.63.18. git tag --contains 4daddec6f200b03a721197d8c0b4b652c994894e | sort -V begins at v2.63.19, matching the advisory; v2.63.18 does not contain the fix.

BIC-only AI check: git cat-file -p 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 contains only tree, parent, human author/committer, and the ordinary commit subject; it has no AI-related trailer or bot identity. AI signals on the squash, PR discussion, later history, or fix were not used.
reasoning: The security invariant in this advisory is not a generic product quota: it is the specific Upload-Length that FileBrowser accepts for one TUS upload. The old io.Copy sink existed earlier, but the exact contradiction—accept and cache a declared length, then write past it and consult it only after writing—first became real in PR #5270 member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5. Its parent directly lacks that accepted-length lifecycle. The member survived through squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e, first released in v2.39.0, and remained exploitable through v2.63.18. Commit 4daddec6f200b03a721197d8c0b4b652c994894e directly closes the write-before-bound flaw and first appears in v2.63.19. Because the true member BIC commit object has neither an AI marker nor a bot identity, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
